subject: economics
objective: Where do demand and supply meet?
instruction: In Harbourview the quantity demanded is Qd = 600 - 5P and the quantity supplied is Qs = -90 + sP. The slope s of the supply curve has not been estimated. Demand is linear, Qd = demand_intercept - demand_slope x P, and supply is linear, Qs = supply_intercept + supply_slope x P, where P is the price in USD and Q is in units. The demand slope is entered as a positive number (the magnitude). Consumer surplus is the triangle between the demand curve and the price up to the equilibrium quantity; producer surplus is the triangle between the price and the supply curve. Required: equilibrium price, equilibrium quantity.
